scope: Inventory of all current open-parent checklist predicates and additional labelled compatibility/recovery follow-ups. This is not the final requirement-by-requirement behavioral audit; Component invariants, detailed plans and all specified acceptance deliverables remain binding. No checklist or parent is closed by this file.
identity_policy: Requirement text hashes prevent silently reusing earlier ordinal IDs after new rows are inserted. Historical roadmap checkmarks are not final38 artifact attestations.

target.admission_observation: Confirmed live by handle polling; no terminal rebuild result.

remaining_evidence_lanes: Terminal official38 lifecycle admission and exact receipt/artifact binding; guarded current-lock container staging and actual image payload/runtime binding.
Complete current38 core/migration/relocation/auth/fault matrix, including separately retained failed attempts and justified unchanged-deadline follow-ups.
Complete current38 controlled/SDK compatibility, public History cold reopen and final privacy scan; full Context8 has separate exact38 evidence.
Current38 native and image Kafka protocol/durability/fairness/retention/cutover/federation regressions and actual coordinator interference.
Current38 native and image desktop/mobile account/OIDC/role/project/eventing/recovery browser regressions, including stale-session401 repair and actual two-rig OpenRig adapter qualification.
Full current38 recovery/initialization/mixed-family/pending-callback/source-query/privacy/crash qualification on native and actual image/platform runtimes.

Current38 actual short-response filter/backend regressions and the fixed independent native/image positive optimizer cohort, preserving all prior negative outcomes and strict per-runtime/aggregate budgets.
Final authority/locks/receipt verification, evidence-to-requirement review, operator/upgrade/rollback/limits documentation, CLI-owned work closure only where every required predicate is proven.

items.title: Partition durable state and migrate single-project installations

requirements.requirement: Add registry, immutable IDs, mutable labels/aliases and explicit active/archive lifecycle; reserve deletion for a separately specified policy.
Partition all data, idempotency, queues, cursors, snapshots, caches and derived state by project; validate references at persistence boundaries.
Implement versioned legacy config/store migration with preflight, backup, interruption recovery and explicit downgrade restrictions.
Coordinate backend/outbox/project key ownership and one recoverable migration sequence with KAFKA-001 and KAFKA-008.

Reject hot removal of the project registry or any admitted project, including dry validation; candidate33 accepted an Admin patch deleting projects and memberships. Preserve complete configuration/revision and retained project data on rejection, including installations without a default project.
Upgrade actual earlier accepted stores and preserve publications, private deliveries, acknowledgements, queries, source IDs and selected optimizer recipes.
Kill/restart migration and project transactions; prove no partial admission, silent empty stores, identity reassignment or cross-project key collisions.

items.title: Enforce project access and agent memberships

requirements.requirement: Add Admin-managed user project access and agent project memberships with stable ownership and explicit project selection.
Enforce role, admission, ownership and membership checks on every direct and indirect operation, including live revocation and queued work.
Preserve local admin bootstrap, OIDC provider links, groups-to-role configuration and non-transitive email correlation; do not import remote access grants.

Prevent a Developer from recreating a removed agent ID that retains private deliveries, receipts, subscriptions or owned jobs in any project. A public-interface probe on candidate31 verified new-owner access to the former owner's private queue. Preserve explicit Admin recovery/reassignment and retained data; add native/container retirement/recreation regression evidence. Candidate32 implements an all-project verified-snapshot guard; native first-install OIDC/accounts checks remain passing in `verification/multi-eventing/oidc-first-setup-32.json`. Independent candidate32 retirement and snapshot-fault suites pass, and role/browser checks pass22 groups. Review found a legacy missing-snapshot path could attempt the bootstrap DETS opener; candidate33 removes that fallback and uses only a verified snapshot server identity. Its legacy/fault requalification and official artifact/image admission remain required.
Exercise the role/owner/project matrix through API and browser, including guessed IDs, forged scopes, stale sessions, token rotation and revocation during work.

items.title: Scope agent coordination and evidence workflows to projects

requirements.requirement: Scope publish/get/search/send/subscribe/poll/ack, source deduplication, corrections and reference traversal; prevent cross-project references from granting visibility.
Scope history/retrieval/archive jobs, feedback/cohorts/replay, optimizer training/evaluation/selection and all caches, snapshots and cancellation.
Add explicit authorized local project discovery and cross-project query fan-out with per-project coverage, deadlines, incremental results and revocation handling.
Apply KAFKA-001's raw/filtered subscription boundaries; integrate the A2A Kafka bridge and independent fact-history projection through KAFKA-003 and KAFKA-005.
Run interleaved projects with identical local IDs and content; prove delivery, deduplication, evidence, replay and optimizer isolation.
Prove explicit fan-out returns only admitted project evidence with accurate partial coverage and no private addressed messages.
Version directory discovery, per-project catalogs, canonical claims, peer trust grants and identity correlation; cache by stable server/project/revision.
Bind durable requests, status polling, responses and idempotency to authenticated origin server plus origin and destination projects; reject scope substitution and stale authority.
Handle same-server canonical routing, conflicts, project archival, peer revocation and negotiated legacy peers without duplicate delivery or silent downgrade.
Qualify at least three real servers with multiple projects, local/remote canonical routing, conflicting owners, stale caches, outages, retries and revocation.
Validate exact new wire traffic independently and test old/new peer compatibility, bounded forwarding, privacy and unchanged server-local roles.

items.title: Manage multiple projects through the hot Admin console

requirements.requirement: Add accessible project creation/switching/rename/archive forms, user/agent access management and per-project catalog/export controls.
Distinguish server-wide users, roles, OIDC, listener/model resources and defaults from project overrides with explicit inheritance and reset semantics.

Scope all views/actions, clear stale browser context on project switching/revocation and preserve confirmation, secret handling, CSRF and concurrent-edit checks. Refresh must reload the admitted project list and names before requesting the selected project; externally removed access must clear the old selection and pending actions.

Repair first-time OIDC setup so the Admin connection test is available for proposed settings before initial save; the inherited browser regression found the button hidden until a provider was already configured. Requalify the corrected artifact and image.

Diagnose and repair the [unexpected HTTP401 in the exact-image foundation browser flow](../../verification/multi-eventing/foundation-browser-34-failure.json). A [deterministic actual-service probe](../../verification/multi-eventing/admin-stale401-34/manifest.json) now proves that an old list_projects HTTP401 resets a newly authenticated workspace while its server session remains valid. Fence stale auth responses and cancel old-context requests; requalify normal desktop/mobile OIDC setup, linking and logout without ignoring unexpected errors. The original untraced401 is not definitively attributed. [Native development35ui qualification](../../verification/multi-eventing/admin-session-35/manifest.json) now passes the strict race regression on both viewports, current-session revocation, the unchanged accounts/OIDC browser suite and18 native cases; the same race harness fails actualimage34. Successor artifact admission and image/browser qualification remain required.
Inspect desktop/mobile flows for every role; exercise concurrent tabs, stale revisions, project switching, live OIDC/access changes and project archival without restart.

items.title: Bound shared resources and operate project lifecycles

requirements.requirement: Specify fair scheduling and accounting across projects and job classes, bounded queues/caches/storage and backpressure.
Fence workers against project archival, access changes and configuration revisions; preserve durable accepted work with explicit terminal/paused states.
Add project-aware diagnostics/audit records and documented full-server and project backup/restore semantics, collision handling and container recovery.

Implement selective recovery into a missing or logically empty target under its original server/project identity, with an Admin plan, complete ownership/reference validation, target-only durable storage/Kafka generations and worker fencing. Preserve every other current project and current global configuration; reject populated logical targets. Follow [the project recovery plan](project-restore.md). The closed recovery authority in `components/hub/project-recovery/spec.md` and [87 independent wire vectors plus six examples](../../verification/project-recovery/contracts.json) are reviewed. Storage registry/bundle verification, Admin jobs, fresh allocation and transport generations, and worker fences are in progress; [five allocator development checks](../../verification/project-recovery/allocator-development.json) pass without claiming integrated recovery. The [development integration checkpoint](../../verification/project-recovery/integration-development.json) records allocator, callback/ticket fences and Admin recovery UI seams; [Nine frozen native component checks](../../verification/project-recovery/components/manifest.json) now pass for nested origin fences, active/queued target tickets, transport reset and pending-work preservation; the decision coordinator compiles. Guarded native development12 now passes18 regression cases and five actual private restore checks; the checkpoint guard passes82 vectors on each of OTP27 and OTP29, and six actual hostile offline rebind cases reject without metadata changes. Native development13 also passes six authenticated federation HTTP checks, including recovery503/Retry-After. The full twelve-boundary crash matrix, actual late network callbacks, broad successor regressions and formal artifact/image/platform qualification remain open. Full-server restore does not discharge this requirement.
Saturate one project with slow/failing model and peer work; demonstrate bounded progress for another and truthful costs/coverage.
Exercise hot lifecycle changes, worker crashes, restart, container replacement and backup/restore without leakage or duplicated committed results.

items.title: Qualify and document the multiple-project upgrade

requirements.requirement: Complete local OCI staging of the locked normative hub specification closure, including the recovery JSON Schema, and allow explicit selection of the verifier CLI/interpreter. The current Markdown-only walker omits declared JSON authority and an ambient CLI can differ from the project-pinned framework. Preserve existing aliases and deterministic archives; reject changed, missing, redirected or colliding inputs and qualify the exact staged byte identities before successor image claims. This is local deployment packaging, not a native-package or registry release.
Update normative specs/traceability, schemas/OpenAPI/examples, agent onboarding, configuration tooling, deployment and operator recovery guides.
Run the complete multiple-project matrix plus existing regression suites against native and Docker artifacts and the existing model container.
Record acceptance identities, upgrade/rollback limitations and unresolved gates; close dependent items and the detailed roadmap only when their evidence passes.

Qualify real oldest-producer0664 and historical snapshot permissions, exact bytes/IDs/acks/retries and cold restart; repair a copy of the actual interrupted prepared migration; prove malformed/foreign/wrong-project/symlink/hardlink/non-owned inputs retain bytes/mode/inode and open no native checkpoint. Recheck strict imported-bundle permission rejection; bind evidence to the repaired successor without relabeling source16.

Verify locked normative staging closure and explicit verifier argv construction with independent byte/determinism/collision/symlink tests. The [construction-only proof](../../verification/project-recovery/development16/staging-closure-review.json) passes14 tests and includes all33 locked specifications; actual successor receipt-bound staging and image qualification remain pending.
Demonstrate two agents coordinating in each of two projects on one server, a multi-project agent and a denied third project, plus a multi-server discovery/canonical-routing scenario.
Run declared lifecycle verification and independent wire/privacy/migration/browser/fairness checks with reproducible artifact-bound reports.

additional_prose_followups.text: - **Local legacy adoption compatibility follow-up:** The oldest supported actual producer writes a valid closed schema1 checkpoint with historical mode0664 and no persisted server ID; successor16 applies imported-bundle private-mode checks during local identity probing and registry adoption, rejecting the unchanged accepted source. Keep bundle/import checks strict and preserve source16. In a separate derived successor, add an explicit local-only bounded owned regular/nlink1/no-symlink reader, safe checkpoint/snapshot preflight and project/server proof; create only private verified staged generations before native opening, retaining original files and migration rollback backups unchanged. Source37 now has component, file-proof, native and actual interrupted-upgrade/cold-replacement evidence; its four SDK ladders pass, while the additional schema2 identity case below requires successor38. Final native, lifecycle, image and platform qualification remain open.

- **Pre-federation schema2 compatibility:** Source37 passes all four SDK producer ladders and seven current context groups, but the existing Context suite's second supported historical producer also lacks a persisted server ID. Its actual closed schema2 checkpoint passes pure physical parsing and complete graph validation; source37 rejects only because its identity genesis guard permits schema1 alone. Extend verified historical absence to schema1 and schema2 in a new immutable successor. Keep schema3-and-later missing IDs, malformed or conflicting IDs, unclosed-checkpoint rules and imported-bundle permissions fail closed. Retain the source37 failure and qualify both historical producers through upgrade and cold restart before claiming the full context suite.

- **Accepted pending-query backup follow-up:** An untouched runtime backup containing pending source/discovery jobs fails RESTORE_INVALID_BACKUP/schema before activation. Diagnosis finds the private validator ignored typeless string constraints, causing both `Scope.host` oneOf branches to match a valid DNS host; the same issue ignores typeless numeric and array bounds. Apply JSON Schema keywords to instances of their matching types regardless of explicit type declarations, enforce IPv6 format and exact oneOf cardinality, and qualify actual accepted-query state plus negative host/limit vectors. Do not skip validation or widen the published source grammar.

- **Pending source-query restart follow-up:** Native14 turns an already dispatched pending SourceQuery into partial/unavailable during origin restart while its original120-second deadline still has more than71 seconds left, current grants/configuration are byte-identical and the actual remote job has completed. Expired/revalidating catalog metadata must not terminalize an already pinned accepted job by itself: retain its ID, owner and deadline, wait for a fresh canonical revalidation and resume the original idempotent peer job. Keep new-query unavailable responses, explicit revocation/removal, identity conflicts and deadline expiry fail closed; never dispatch through stale metadata or a replacement owner. Preserve the failing actual pre-restore witness and qualify same-ID old/fresh callbacks independently.

- **Target isolation follow-up:** Actual native14 corruption acceptance passes checksum, stale snapshot, foreign identity, missing checkpoint and damaged checkpoint cases with global Admin and newer Blue state still available. A registered target snapshot symlink still stops the whole hub. Preserve that failure and quarantine only its validated registered target without opening/following the path; keep shared registry/marker/decision corruption globally fail closed. Uninitialized entries must retain that status only while both selected files are exactly absent. Also qualify initialization after a hot relocation makes the former root inaccessible; empty entries must not remain anchored there.

- **Live callback follow-up:** The real Kafka consumer-response fixture on development13 restores its target successfully but the old eventing worker logs `RECOVERY_REQUIRED` and exits; the per-project worker-start guard then prevents transport progress. Preserve this run, keep the eventing loop alive across a retired work unit, and notify the waiting owner when an active HTTP ticket is retired so it can begin a fresh epoch promptly. The [two-module native repair](../../verification/project-recovery-pending-kafka/manifest.json) now passes five actual broker callback/ack/restart checks; the [exact combined14 rerun](../../verification/project-recovery-pending-kafka/native14-manifest.json) also passes all five checks.

- **Successor admission preparation:** Reconcile the installed framework distribution with the pinned Standard through the reviewed CLI flow before lock/recipe refresh; do not hand-edit the pin, locks or receipt. Regenerate native-test and source-BOM metadata for the recovery modules. Keep Makefile dependency declarations identical to the assembler source closure; staging review found `resources.exs` omitted from `SRCS` although it was already assembled. Its declared clean target also lacked `tools/clean.exs`; restore the unchanged protected helper from source34 before staging, and verify only owned output directories are removed.

- **Kafka transport progress repair:** The unchanged native14 hot-move test exceeds its20-second raw-fanout bound although broker produce/offset/commit requests take roughly10–20ms. Duration-only copies trace the delay to shared HTTP client keepalive sessions behind one-second consumer long polls, with Resource acquisition and Store work remaining bounded. An otherwise identical copy using isolated closing Eventing HTTP sessions passes all seven original cases, including the same20-second fanout gate,16 concurrent writes and cold recovery. Apply that transport isolation without changing broker success bodies, resource caps, model networking or deadlines; qualify final combined runtime and verify closing-session lifecycle.

- **Successor regression follow-up:** Frozen development13 passes fresh explicit Admin initialization and authentication setup, but changing `store_path` to a fresh root returns `503 CONFIG_WRITE_FAILED`. Diagnose and repair registry-selected generation relocation, retain the original failed foundation/store-move runs, then rerun exact hot-move, collision, interrupted-move and cold-restart cases. The repaired native14 now completes hot relocation, but its original concurrent fanout deadline still fails despite observed broker progress; preserve and diagnose that result before closure. Source13 stays immutable; no successor migration closure is claimed.

items.title: Integrate per-server Kafka with durable event publication

requirements.requirement: Provision documented internal topics/partitions and authentication/ACL boundaries; keep private addressed messages and credentials outside public event topics.
Implement durable publish acceptance, retry/deduplication, consumer checkpoints and health/backpressure under broker outages.
Fence consumers and topic lifecycle against project archive, restore, credential rotation and configuration revisions.
Kill hub/broker around each publish/checkpoint boundary; prove no acknowledged event is lost and retries do not create duplicate logical publications.
Exercise multi-project isolation, rebalances, broker unavailability, disk/queue limits and recovery with a real Kafka service.

items.title: Bridge Kafka subscriptions to durable A2A deliveries

requirements.requirement: Add explicit project subscriptions with optional deterministic selectors and no required model/description; preserve legacy described subscriptions as filtered mode.
Persist independent subscription progress and recipient deliveries; separate broker processing offsets from agent acknowledgements and handle out-of-order ack safely.

Define overlapping-subscription deduplication, unsubscribe/pause/resume, offline consumers, bounded replay and explicit retention-gap handling without weakening existing unacknowledged-delivery durability.
Run official A2A SDK flows with multiple subscribers receiving every project event and no direct broker access; prove zero model calls.
Exercise disconnect/reconnect, concurrent subscribe/publish, filter changes, repeated polls/acks, overlapping subscriptions and consumer rebalances.

items.title: Apply optional Jev-like filters without blocking raw streams

requirements.requirement: Define filter enable/disable/edit revisions, threshold policy, input context and durable retry/backlog state; use deterministic selectors before inference.

Add isolated queues, fairness, timeouts, per-project/subscription budgets and filter-decision provenance without inventing probabilities for raw deliveries. Current integration bounds the model-ready queue and retains overflow as deferred frozen targets in original durable event state; raw fanout must continue and diagnostics must distinguish ready, deferred and paused work.
Make the model provider optional at startup; expose unsupported/unavailable filtered subscriptions explicitly and preserve accepted pending decisions across recovery.
With no model configured and with a hung/failing model, prove raw subscriptions deliver promptly with zero inference calls and other projects are not starved.
Validate real short-response filtered matches/nonmatches, malformed decisions, retries, hot filter edits and revocation without silent misses or duplicated deliveries.

items.title: Preserve backend fact search independently of pubsub

requirements.requirement: Define backend/index ingestion watermarks and read-after-publish/search visibility; recover projection lag without treating missing indexed facts as negative evidence.
Preserve original history after broker retention, filter rejection, delivery acknowledgement and subscriber removal; keep private messages excluded.
Decouple search/model workers and readiness from raw eventing, adapting replay/cohorts/optimizer evidence to project-scoped event identities and optional models.
Publish with no model and no subscriptions; prove facts remain searchable after filtering, acknowledgements, restart and broker log expiry.
Exercise lag/rebuild/restore and model-disabled semantic queries with truthful coverage and unchanged evidence/privacy guarantees.

items.title: Expose hot Kafka and subscription controls in Admin

requirements.requirement: Add normal forms for raw versus filtered subscriptions, filter health/backlogs and project-wide event observation. Provide confirmed revisioned subscription edits, pause/resume and selector/filter changes through Admin; preserve queued deliveries and acknowledgements.

Provide hot connection/credential/topic-policy changes with validation, cutover watermarks, consumer fencing and rollback; forbid silent resets or implicit replay. Recovery forms must support explicit subscription IDs/revisions beyond the bounded first page, with no hidden replay target truncation. Current integration is completing partial per-project topic-prefix, retention and backlog-policy overrides with explicit inheritance; broker endpoint, security and enabled state remain server-wide. Qualify failed multi-project retention proposals against actual broker state before closing this control gate.

Qualify interruption recovery of the new durable all-project transport transition and implement explicit Admin quarantine repair; candidate10 already passes real-Kafka successful/failed cutover and hard restart, linked in the partial progress record.
Expose authorized broker lag, outbox/projection backlog, retention gaps, budgets and delivery/model status with secret redaction and server/project scope.
Inspect desktop/mobile role-scoped flows, stale revisions, CSRF, access revocation and model on/off transitions.
Rotate broker credentials and change connection/filter settings live under load; prove no hub restart, lost accepted work or cross-project exposure.

items.title: Package per-server Kafka for containers and Kubernetes

requirements.requirement: Select pinned Kafka/KRaft images and client compatibility; declare dependencies, persistent volumes, private listeners, secrets, resource limits and readiness/startup/shutdown ordering. Generate and retain a distinct installation cluster ID, preserving existing volume metadata rather than assigning the tutorial cluster ID to every deployment.
Provide Compose and Kubernetes packaging with model-free baseline and optional existing model/GPU service or configured remote model; choose and document Kubernetes manifest/chart ownership.
Document single-node versus replicated broker durability, single-writer hub replica limits, backup/restore, rolling broker upgrades and hot hub configuration propagation.
Boot clean Compose and disposable Kubernetes deployments with real Kafka and no model; run A2A pub/sub and backend search smoke tests.
Exercise replacement/restart, PVC or volume reuse, broker failure/upgrade, secret rotation and optional-model enablement; validate manifests and image/dependency/license inventories.

items.title: Migrate existing subscriptions and queues to Kafka safely

requirements.requirement: Specify ordered schema/config upgrades, cutover watermarks and topic initialization for legacy and already multi-project stores.
Reconcile durable outbox, Kafka offsets, pending model jobs, deliveries and backend projection state without replaying old publications as newly subscribed events.
Provide preflight, backups, resumable migration markers, abort/recovery and explicit downgrade restrictions for store plus broker state.
Migrate actual earlier accepted stores with offline agents, pending filters, duplicate retries and acknowledged deliveries; compare identities and counts.
Inject crashes at every cutover boundary and restore backups; prove no silent loss, unsolicited history replay, cross-project leakage or double delivery.

items.title: Qualify Kafka pubsub and update all operating contracts

requirements.requirement: Update normative Component contracts, schemas/OpenAPI/examples, client onboarding, traceability, deployment and troubleshooting guides together.
Run zero-model raw-subscription/search acceptance and separate live-model filtered/semantic-query acceptance plus multi-project and federated regressions.
Verify durable handoffs, fanout, fairness, retention/replay gaps and fault recovery at documented limits; record exact artifact/image/broker/client identities.
Demonstrate two projects with multiple publishers and independent raw/filtered subscribers, an unauthorized project and a federated peer using its own Kafka.
Pass declared verification and independent wire/privacy/fault/migration/deployment suites; document remaining limits and publication gates before closure.

items.title: Support OpenRig cross-rig communication through ADHD

requirements.requirement: Inspect and pin the supported OpenRig release/API; specify stable rig/agent identity, ADHD project mapping and a minimal A2A adapter or skill where needed.
Provide setup for agents in separate OpenRig rigs to publish/subscribe, send/poll/acknowledge and search through one ADHD hub, then through federated hubs with canonical routing.
Preserve project admission, owner/role boundaries, provenance, retries and loop/duplicate prevention; keep rig identity as provenance rather than an automatic access grant.
Document supported versions, credential provisioning, recovery and the division of responsibility; retain support for agents outside OpenRig.

Run two actual OpenRig rigs with independently authenticated agents: verify cross-rig raw events with zero inference, direct messages, acknowledgements and backend search; include an optional plain-text filter case.

Verify offline/restart/retry recovery and denial of unauthorized projects, then exercise two rigs using separate federated ADHD servers with exact rig/agent/project/source provenance and no transferred roles.
